q: 1. The relation between modulus of rupture fcr, splitting strength fcs and direct tensile strength ft is given by ...........
explain: The modulus of rupture (flexural strength) is always highest, followed by splitting tensile strength, with direct tensile strength being the lowest.

q: 2. The compressive strength of 100 mm cube as compared to 150 mm cube is always ...........
explain: Smaller specimen sizes usually exhibit higher apparent compressive strength because of reduced probability of critical flaws and different end-restraint effects.

q: 3. According to I.S.: 456-1978, the modulus of elasticity of concrete Ec (in N/mm2) can be taken as ...........
explain: The older version of the code (IS 456:1978) specified 5700 * sqrt(fck); note that the 2000 version uses 5000 * sqrt(fck).

q: 4. Admixtures which cause early setting, and hardening of concrete are called ...........
explain: Accelerators are chemicals that speed up the chemical reaction of cement with water, reducing setting time and increasing early strength.

q: 5. In reinforced cement concrete structures, the steel reinforcement consists of ...........
options: mild steel and medium tensile steel bars
explain: Reinforced concrete can utilize various types of steel reinforcement including mild steel, CTD, and modern TMT (deformed) bars.

q: 6. In the limit state method, the compressive force in concrete is taken to act at a distance of ...... times the neutral axis measured from the extreme compression fibre.
explain: Based on the parabolic-rectangular stress block used in IS:456, the centroid of the compressive force is 0.42 times the depth of the neutral axis (xu).

q: 7. Modular ratio in reinforced concrete is defined as ...........
options: Modulus of elasticity of steel / Modulus of elasticity of concrete
Modulus of elasticity of concrete / Modulus of elasticity of steel
Coefficient of linear expansion steel / Coefficient of linear expansion of concrete
explain: Modular ratio (m) is the ratio of the Modulus of Elasticity of Steel (Es) to the Modulus of Elasticity of Concrete (Ec).

q: 8. M 15 grade of concrete approximates ...........
explain: M15 concrete is typically mixed in the ratio of 1:2:4 (Cement:Sand:Aggregate).

q: 9. M 25 grade of concrete approximates ...........
explain: For M25, the nominal mix is approximately 1:1:2, though higher grades usually require design mixes.

q: 10. The design strength of the materials in the limit state method is given by ...........
explain: Design strength = Characteristic Strength (f) divided by Partial Safety Factor (γm).

q: 11. The shape stress-strain curve of mild steel up to yield stress is ...........
explain: Mild steel is a linearly elastic material up to its yield point, meaning stress is directly proportional to strain.

q: 12. The ultimate tensile stress in mild steel bars of grade I should be greater than (in N/mm2) ...........
explain: Grade I mild steel typically has an ultimate tensile strength exceeding 415 N/mm², even if its yield stress is lower (around 250 N/mm²).

q: 13. In the limit state method the over-reinforced sections ...........
options: are permitted only in extreme cases
explain: Limit State Design strictly prohibits over-reinforced sections to ensure that failure is always ductile (steel yields before concrete crushes).

q: 14. In the limit state method, the maximum compressive strain in axial compression in concrete is taken as ...........
explain: While 0.0035 is for flexure, in cases of pure axial compression, the failure strain across the entire section is taken as 0.002.

q: 15. The section of a reinforced beam where most distant concrete fibre in compression and tension in steel attains permissible stresses simultaneously, is called ...........
explain: A balanced section is also known as a critical section (where neutral axis is at critical depth) and is often the most economical in terms of material usage.

q: 16. In a singly reinforced beam, if the permissible stress in concrete reaches earlier than that in steel, the beam section is called ...........
explain: If concrete reaches its limit first, it means there is 'too much' steel for the concrete to handle, hence 'over-reinforced'.

q: 17. As the percentage of steel increases ............
explain: In a reinforced concrete beam, the depth of the neutral axis is directly proportional to the reinforcement ratio. Increasing the steel area requires a larger concrete compression area to maintain equilibrium, thus pushing the neutral axis deeper.

q: 18. Distribution of shear intensity over a rectangular section of a beam, follows ............
explain: For a homogenous rectangular section, the shear stress distribution is parabolic, with the maximum stress occurring at the neutral axis and zero at the top and bottom fibers.

q: 19. In singly reinforced beams, steel reinforcement is provided in ............
explain: A singly reinforced beam is designed such that the steel is only placed in the tension zone to resist tensile stresses which concrete cannot.

q: 20. In a simply supported reinforced concrete beam, the reinforcement is placed ............
explain: In a simply supported beam, sagging occurs, meaning the bottom fibers are in tension. Therefore, reinforcement is placed below the neutral axis.

q: 21. The section in which concrete is not fully stressed to its permissible value when stress in steel reaches its maximum value, is called ............
explain: In an under-reinforced section, the steel reaches its yield point first while the concrete stress remains below its ultimate capacity.

q: 22. The neutral axis of a balanced section is called ............
explain: The depth of the neutral axis corresponding to the balanced strain/stress condition is termed the Critical Neutral Axis.

q: 23. The section of the beam having greater width at the top in comparison to the width below neutral axis is known as
explain: A T-beam consists of a wide top flange (which handles compression) and a narrow rib below (the web), resulting in a wider top than bottom.

q: 24. In a T-beam, the vertical distance between the bottom of the flange and the centre of the tensile reinforcement is known as the
explain: The 'rib' or 'web' is the portion of the beam below the flange. The vertical distance from the underside of the flange to the reinforcement level is essentially the depth of the rib.

q: 25. The assumed overall depth of the T-beam is taken as... of the span when it is supported t ends.
explain: For initial trial sizing of a simply supported T-beam, the overall depth is generally assumed to be between 1/12 and 1/15 of the span.

q: 26. The width of the flange of L-beam, should be less than
options: breadth of the rib + four times thickness of the slab
breadth of the rib + half clear distance between ribs
explain: Similar to T-beams, L-beams have specific geometric limits in the code for 'effective width'—usually based on span, rib width, and slab thickness.

q: 27. A reinforced concrete beam is design to resist
explain: A complete beam design must account for flexural tension (steel), flexural compression (concrete/steel), and shear (stirrups).

q: 28. Steel is very strong
explain: While steel can handle both, its primary purpose in RCC is its high tensile strength to compensate for concrete's weakness.

q: 29. At cracked concrete stage of a reinforced concrete beam, the maximum tensile stress in concrete remains
options: less than its modulus of rupture
more than its modulus of rupture
explain: Concrete cracks once the tensile stress exceeds its Modulus of Rupture (flexural tensile strength).

q: 30. The analysis and design of reinforced concrete beam at the cracked concrete stage is done by
explain: The Working Stress Method (WSM) is based on the elastic theory and assumes the concrete is cracked and the steel carries all tension, focusing on serviceability at the cracked stage.

q: 31. Compression failure of simply reinforced beam occurs in
explain: In an over-reinforced beam, the concrete reaches its crushing strain before the steel yields, leading to a sudden, brittle compression failure.

q: 32. Yielding of steel in singly reinforced beam occurs in
explain: Yielding of steel is the defining characteristic of an under-reinforced section, ensuring a ductile failure mode.

q: 33. The limiting moment of resistance for a singly reinforced beam using Fe 250 steel and general grade concrete, is
explain: For Fe 250 steel (mild steel), the limiting moment of resistance factor (Mu,lim) is 0.148 (rounded to 0.149 in some texts) times fck·bd².

q: 34. To ensure that under the applied moment the concrete and steel in singly reinforced beam reach their stresses, the minimum area of steel
explain: As per IS 456, the minimum tension reinforcement (As) is given by As/bd = 0.85/fy.

q: 35. The strain at the level of compression reinforcement is doubly reinforced beam is
explain: From the strain triangle, the strain at depth d' is linearly proportional to the distance from the neutral axis: εsc = 0.0035 * (xu - d') / xu.

q: 36. For design purpose of flexural members, the compressive strength of concrete is assumed to be
explain: Design strength = (0.67 * fck) / 1.5 (Partial Safety Factor) ≈ 0.446 fck, often simplified or rounded to 0.42-0.45 in various literature batches.

q: 37. For simply supported slabs spanning in one direction, the ratio of span to overall depth should exceed
explain: For slabs, the span/overall depth ratio is typically kept around 25-30 for simply supported spans to control deflection.

q: 38. The ultimate strength of a balanced reinforced concrete beam is proportional to
options: crushing strength of an and/or tensile strength of the steel
explain: In a balanced section, both concrete and steel reach their limits simultaneously.

q: 39. The ultimate bending compressive strain allowed in R.C.C. beam is
explain: IS 456 assumes the maximum strain in concrete at the outermost compression fiber is 0.0035 in bending.

q: 40. The secondary compression failure in R.C.C. beam is caused in
explain: In under-reinforced beams, steel yields first, causing the neutral axis to rise until concrete crushes (secondary compression failure).

q: 41. A pre-stressed concrete member
explain: Pre-stressed concrete is defined by the intentional introduction of internal stresses (usually compressive) to counteract the tensile stresses caused by external loads.

q: 42. Columns may be made of plain concrete of their unsupported length do not exceed their least lateral dimension
explain: According to IS 456, a compression member is called a 'pedestal' if its unsupported length is less than 3 times its least lateral dimension; these can be plain concrete.

q: 43. The modular ratio m of a concrete whose permissible compressive stress is C, may be obtained from the equation
explain: The standard IS 456 formula for the modular ratio in Working Stress Method is m = 280 / (3 * sigma_cbc), where C is the permissible stress.

q: 44. If the ratio of the span to the overall depth does not exceed 10, the stiffness of the beam will ordinarily be satisfactory in case of a
explain: Cantilever beams are most critical for deflection; keeping L/D ≤ 10 (or specifically 7 for basic limits) usually ensures adequate stiffness.
